newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE studies power, water privatisation.
newsitem.headline: UAE studies power, water privatisation.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates is studying the possible privatisation of its power and water sectors, but not if this means a burden on consumers, Minister of Water and Electricity Hamid Nasser al-Oweiss said.

"We have the vision to develop private sector support, however the criteria for privatisation has yet to be set," he said in a paper prepared for the Middle East Infrastructure Development Congress which ends in Dubai on Tuesday.
"We support the privatisation process if it has clear economic dimensions and leads to improvement and betterment of services and reduces costs to consumers.
"But if its objective is to obtain immediate revenues at cost to the consumer or public sector, we will not proceed, because privatisation should not prove to be a burden on consumers," he said
Last year the UAE raised power rates by 33 percent, but electricity and water are still heavily subsidised.
The UAE, like its Gulf Arab allies, has spent hundreds of millions of dollars in recent years on power generation and water desalination plants to keep up with fast rising demand.
